lockup.summary: Officers, directors and holders of nearly all shares agreed not to sell for 180 days after the prospectus date. The two co-founders and their related entities agreed to 270 days.

what: It makes Curodont, a peptide-based treatment that repairs early tooth cavities and helps keep the natural tooth.
proceeds: It expects about $154.5 million in net proceeds. It plans to use the money for general business needs such as working capital, operating costs and equipment, and it may use some to buy other businesses.
risks: The company's success depends on dentists and patients accepting and understanding Curodont, a new kind of cavity treatment.
Its results depend on distributors, especially Henry Schein, and on large customers such as Heartland.
Growing revenue depends on building up its sales and marketing team.
It may have trouble managing its fast growth.
It relies on outside companies to make, supply and assemble its products.
